summary: @c1-ease/autoloan postinstall beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded VPS
details: The package ships a postinstall script `node beacon.cjs` that collects os.hostname(), the install path (__dirname), process.cwd(), and the Node.js version and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded non-first-party endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc with TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). The same beacon is invoked again at require-time from index.js, so the exfiltration fires both on `npm install` and whenever the module is loaded. index.js itself exports a Proxy that returns a no-op function for any property access, giving the package no functional behavior beyond preventing consumer builds from crashing while the beacon runs. The scoped name `@c1-ease/autoloan`, the stub Proxy facade, and the hardcoded Contabo VPS destination are the shape of a dependency-confusion probe against an internal package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
